newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SOCIALISTS DENY SELLOFF CASE INVOLVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SOCIALISTS DENY SELLOFF CASE INVOLVEMENT.

text.p: Socialist party officials have denied that the party is involved in Hungary's 1996 privatisation scandal also known as the "Tocsik affair".
"The party...reaffirms that its budget did not and does not contain any illegal or unclear incomes," a party steering committee statement said on Saturday.
On Monday Hungary's Chief Prosecutor Kalman Gyorgyi asked Parliament to lift Socialist Party treasurer Laszlo Boldvai's parliamentary immunity following evidence that may implicate him in the affair.

A Budapest court started on Wednesday proceedings in the Tocsik affair, in which an adviser to state privatisation agency APV Marta Tocsik received $5 million for negotiating land deals with municipalities on APV's behalf.
Revelations of the payments led Horn to dismiss last October the entire APV board and the minister in charge of privatisation, Tamas Suchman.

Gyorgyi's letter to Parliament said Boldvai and Gyorgy Budai, a businessman with close ties to junior coalition Free Democrats, told Tocsik that she could keep an installment of her success fee if she transferred 25 percent each to accounts the two men named, which she did.
Ferenc Baja, President of the Socialists' steering committee said Boldvai is looking forward to the court proceedings to clarify the issue.
"He has nothing to hide and is expecting the chance to clear his name," Baja said.
